utterances.text: Okay. You didn't know there were Main Staff plans that called for use of the MUP, in May, to liberate, to create conditions for the liberation of the enclaves?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: No. Can you please clarify what form did these plans have? They were never sent to us, nor did I have any opportunity to discuss such plans at Supreme Command meetings that I may have attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just move on to July.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P04484?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, this is a tape of a conversation between Radovan Karadzic and the person who just testified before you, Drina Corps Commander Zivanovic, on 8 July. Now, if you look on your version, Karadzic says further down, after asking how things are going. Fine. So I can't give any of the - it's unintelligible - to you. Everything is taken and only if you need any large ones. It should be checked through the Main Staff. I know that there is some and where it is, so we could probably reinforce you a little. And Zivanovic says: We will also need that. Karadzic says: Pardon? And Zivanovic says: That will also be much needed. And Karadzic says: All right. Call the Main Staff up there and I know that it came in, and you can call me via Barijera and then we can talk and reinforce. Then if we go to page 2 of the English, Karadzic says: All right, just tell Krle that I can't get to him right now. Well, the entire MUP is engaged. I really don't have these from Zvornik or the last reserves of these in Sarajevo, at Treskavica, in fact at Trnovo. Zivanovic says: Yes. Karadzic: So there is no other way, you have to go with your own forces. Zivanovic: Yes. And then says that they need to be careful speaking on the phone. So the day before you met with General Karadzic -- with President Karadzic, the Drina Corps commander had requested MUP forces; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. He did not ask them from me. I can see from this transcript that he did ask for them, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: He didn't ask them from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's have P04930, please. This is a Drina Corps command document from 8 July, an urgent regular combat report. Again 8 July, from General Zivanovic. Page 2 of the English, please, as well as the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Look at number 9, Mr Kovac: "Due to the possibility of enemy attacks in the north-west part of the front, particularly from Kalesija, Kladanj, all other directions," I won't read the whole thing, "please engage MUP forces from Zvornik, their 1st Company, through the RS MUP as reserve forces for the 1st Birac Infantry Brigade to help on this endangered axis." So it's not correct, is it, that General Krstic -- that Karadzic came up with this idea, meeting with you on the 9 July, to save face, saying, Please, General Krstic, ask for some units from the MUP so that I look like I'm involved in Srebrenica and get some credit. The Drina Corps had requested these units the day before. You know that now; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: No. That's not right. First of all, I know what President Karadzic told me directly when he asked me to provide two special units to go to Srebrenica. What you are talking about, and what General Zivanovic is requesting, the engagement of police forces, this position is about 150 kilometres away from Srebrenica, so we cannot even join it or link it with their action focused on Srebrenica. This has to do with the overall activities of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, if we know Olovo is certainly 150 kilometres from Srebrenica and Kladanj also 120 kilometres, Kalesija is the closest. It's also around 120 kilometres. So one cannot connect this with the Srebrenica operation. This is the protection of lines at completely different part of the theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's concerned about attacks on the Zvornik Brigade, it says, and enemy attacks in this area on the Zvornik Brigade, and the Zvornik Brigade is asking for the 1st Company from Zvornik. And what the Zvornik Brigade is doing on 8 July is day 2 of the attack on Srebrenica; correct? Day 3, actually?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Look here, one thing is where the Zvornik Brigade was engaged and their defence lines are something else. The defence lines of the Zvornik Brigade were on average 100 to 150 kilometres away from Srebrenica, where they were in combat engagement in connection with the Srebrenica action, and because these lines were weakened, we had those requests that they be assisted there. Even the town of Zvornik at the time was completely unprotected, which can be seen from a series of dispatches. So let us not mix the defence line of the Zvornik Brigade, which is something quite different, as a position, and their combat engagement, a part of their brigade or most of their brigade, in the Srebrenica action.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Nevertheless, 1st Company was engaged and took part in the Srebrenica action; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: The 1st Company was singled out on the president's orders, and resubordinated to Ljubisa Borovcanin, who was subordinated to the army, and they were engaged in the area of Srebrenica. But I think that that was only on the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We'll get to that in a minute. And you've also said in your statements and in many of your interviews that at this time you were focused basically exclusively on Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the other microphone for counsel please be switched on? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have 06421, please? Is this P06421? That's better. Thank you. That's the correct document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I think you've seen this document before, Mr Kovac. This is the 6th of July. It's from the RS Ministry of Interior police force headquarters Pale. It's type signed from you, as Staff Commander, and it reports first on what's going on with the Herzegovina Corps and discusses how many enemy soldiers were killed and how many were captured. Then if we turn the page in the English, we get to reporting on the Trnovo area, then we get to reporting on Novi, and then at the bottom you report: "In the early morning hours of 6 July, the offensive against Srebrenica began and we shall provide you with timely information on all interesting developments in that theatre of operations." This covers all areas of interest to the MUP combat at that time, right, including the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: No. This is an exchange of information from the front line between the services of the army, the State Security Service, and the Public Security Service. This is a form of information, you can see Herzegovina, Trnovo, Sarajevo, Krajina, you see the fall of the lines at Krajina, and this last information that an offensive started at Srebrenica, this was sent by the State Security Service and this cannot be linked up in any way to any presence of the MUP forces. This is all normal because all the -- all of these activities are reflected on the area where the police is carrying out their duties in terms of securing the areas in depth. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I didn't ask you with regard to Srebrenica about this was engagement or presence of MUP forces. I said this is you reporting on what's happening in Srebrenica and saying that you shall provide timely information on all interesting developments in that theatre of operations. Right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, the way in which we provide information from the front line has to do with the degree of information that we received from military units, corps or the Main Staff, the extent to which they convey information to us, and what they deem necessary to convey to us in terms of combat operations because this is their line of work, not ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. So we'll get to that in a minute, but these lines of information come to you and as Staff Commander you are reporting it further and saying that you will continue to report?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, most of this -- well, it arrived in functional terms but this was a routine exchange of information, routine information, so this went according to an inertia of daily reporting of the ministry, or, rather, positions, units, that were involved in certain areas, and because of preparations --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. So last time: You, as Staff Commander, are reporting on Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I'm not reporting about Srebrenica. I am conveying information. We are conveying information. We are only conveying information that we received from other services. This is daily information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you're conveying information that you also received from MUP services like state security; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, part of the MUP service, and as far as combat activities are concerned, it's mostly from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. This is regular exchange of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question at all. I'll read it again: And you're conveying information that you also received from MUP services like state security; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I am not conveying it personally. This has to do with the institution of the staff and the institution of the ministry. So this is a form of methodology of work. By all means, all the information that our service receives is forwarded to those to whom they may be of interest in order to take measures within their own remit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: By the staff, this forwarding is by the staff that you command, that you're head of, and it includes information you receive, you, the staff, about Srebrenica. It's plain on the face of your document. Why can't you answer that "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I'm answering clearly to you. You will certainly see a dispatch here that I did not sign. It doesn't really matter whether I signed it. You are accentuating Srebrenica as some special information, and I'm taking it as part of a series of information from the area of Republika Srpska at the time. That is the difference, in terms of my answer, whether I got any special information for Srebrenica. I didn't get it. It's the institution that got it, and we forwarded it, and I don't see anything to be challenged there, that we forwarded that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we adjourn here?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I wasn't sure, if it's three minutes I've got another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, I have a question for Mr. Robinson. It's about Defence motion for order concerning Rule 70 documents from Krajisnik case that has been pending since 13th of May this year. According to the Prosecution submission, which was on the 2nd of August, rule -- the Rule 70 provider had agreed to disclose to the accused the two filings in question, subject to Rule 70 conditions. What's the current status of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we received those filings and so the motion is moot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you will withdraw it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr Kovac, we will continue tomorrow morning at 9.00, so I'd like to advise you not discuss about your testimony with anybody else. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, am I allowed to contact with Mr. Tomislav Kovac while he made his solemn note and he started his evidence? But what I can do, I can just make a promise that I won't discuss the topic regarding this, but he's alone here and I'm the only person that he knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber has no difficulty as long as you do not discuss about his testimony. Do you understand that, sir, Mr Kovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 1st day of November, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.45 p.m.,
